{{one source|date=June 2017}}
In the mathematical theory of probability, '''Blumenthal's [[zero–one law]]''',<ref>{{Citation
 | last = Blumenthal
 | first = Robert M.
 | title = An extended Markov property
 | journal = Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 85
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 52–72
 | year = 1957
 | jstor = 1992961
 | doi = 10.1090/s0002-9947-1957-0088102-2
 | mr = 0088102
 | zbl = 0084.13602| doi-access = free
 }}</ref> named after [[Robert McCallum Blumenthal]], is a statement about the nature of the beginnings of [[right continuous]] [[Feller process]]. Loosely, it states that any [[right continuous]] [[Feller process]] on <math>[0,\infty)</math> starting from deterministic point has also deterministic initial movement.

== Statement ==
Suppose that <math>X=(X_t:t\geq 0)</math> is an adapted [[right continuous]] [[Feller process]] on a [[probability space]] <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_{t}\}_{t\geq 0},\mathbb{P})</math> such that <math>X_0</math> is constant with probability one. Let <math>\mathcal{F}^X_t:=\sigma(X_s; s\leq t), \mathcal{F}^X_{t^+}:=\bigcap_{s>t}\mathcal{F}^X_s</math>. Then any event in the [[Germ (mathematics)|germ]] [[sigma algebra]] <math> \Lambda \in \mathcal{F}^X_{0+}</math>  has either <math>\mathbb{P}(\Lambda)=0</math> or <math>\mathbb{P}(\Lambda)=1.</math>

== Generalization ==
Suppose that <math>X=(X_t:t\geq 0)</math> is an adapted  [[stochastic process]] on a [[probability space]] <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_{t}\}_{t\geq 0},\mathbb{P})</math> such that <math>X_0</math> is constant with probability one. If <math>X</math> has [[Markov property]] with respect to the filtration <math>\{\mathcal{F}_{t^+}\}_{t\geq 0}</math> then any event <math> \Lambda \in \mathcal{F}^X_{0+}</math>  has either <math>\mathbb{P}(\Lambda)=0</math> or <math>\mathbb{P}(\Lambda)=1.</math> Note that every [[right continuous]] [[Feller process]] on a [[probability space]] <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_{t}\}_{t\geq 0},\mathbb{P})</math>  has [[strong Markov property]] with respect to the filtration <math>\{\mathcal{F}_{t^+}\}_{t\geq 0}</math>.
